title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 205 (Functions of company secretary)

content.overview: Section 205 provides that the functions of the company secretary shall include—(a) to report to the Board about compliance with the provisions of this Act, the rules made thereunder and other laws applicable to the company; (b) to ensure that the company complies with the applicable secretarial standards; (c) to discharge such other duties as may be prescribed. Appointment of a company secretary as key managerial personnel in prescribed classes is under section 203; the definition is in section 2(51).
content.glance: CS functions: report to Board on compliance with Act, rules and other applicable laws; ensure compliance with secretarial standards; other prescribed duties; appointment as KMP under s. 203; defined in s. 2(51).
content.study: The functions of the company secretary shall include—(a) to report to the Board about compliance with the provisions of this Act, the rules made thereunder and other laws applicable to the company; (b) to ensure that the company complies with the applicable secretarial standards; (c) to discharge such other duties as may be prescribed. Current-law framing: identify the company secretary; apply the reporting, secretarial-standards and prescribed-duty functions. Appointment obligation for prescribed classes is s. 203; secretarial audit of bigger companies is s. 204. A company secretary is a key managerial person under s. 2(51).

sections.heading: Compliance Reporting
sections.body: Report to the Board about compliance with the Act, the rules and other laws applicable to the company.

sections.heading: Secretarial Standards
sections.body: Ensure that the company complies with the applicable secretarial standards.

sections.heading: Other Prescribed Duties
sections.body: Discharge such other duties as may be prescribed.

sections.heading: Relationship to Appointment
sections.body: Functions are stated in s. 205; mandatory appointment as whole-time KMP in prescribed classes is under s. 203.

examples.title: Secretarial standards not monitored
examples.body: A company secretary fails to ensure compliance with applicable secretarial standards and does not report the gap to the Board. Section 205 expressly includes ensuring secretarial-standard compliance and reporting compliance to the Board.

examples.title: Functions vs appointment
examples.body: A prescribed-class company has no company secretary. The failure is primarily under s. 203 (appointment of KMP). Section 205 states the functions once a CS is in place.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 205 itself require every company to appoint a company secretary?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 205 states the functions of the company secretary. The obligation to appoint a whole-time CS as KMP for prescribed classes is in section 203.

distinctions.title: Functions of CS (s. 205) vs appointment of KMP (s. 203)
distinctions.left: What the CS must do once appointed
distinctions.right: Which companies must appoint a whole-time CS (among other KMP)

misconceptions.trap: Section 205 is only about reporting to the Board; secretarial standards are optional.
misconceptions.correction: Section 205 expressly requires the CS to ensure that the company complies with the applicable secretarial standards, in addition to compliance reporting and other prescribed duties.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 205 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the CS. II. Apply reporting, secretarial-standards and prescribed-duty functions. III. Distinguish appointment under s. 203. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: CS status; functions performed or omitted; precise relief.
